records.name: Adrians
records.facts_used: Adrians is the Latvian form of Adrian, from Roman Hadrianus, from Hadria, a place in Italy. Its origin is geographical: a connection with a place rather than a quality assigned to everyone who bears the name. Emperor Hadrian belongs to the Roman name family. Following his visit to Britain in AD 122, the Roman army began building Hadrian’s Wall on his orders. English Heritage documents this specific monument connected with the imperial name.
